_comment: The single list of skill -> standalone-repo mirror pairs.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The pairing was already written down twice inside
.github/workflows/sync-standalone-skills.yml — once as the matrix and once as the paths:
trigger filter — and a third copy was about to be added. Two hand-maintained lists of the
same thing drift, and this pair drifts in the worst direction: a mirror missing from paths:
never fires, so the standalone silently stops updating while CI stays green.
This file is the source of truth. scripts/ci/standalone-mirror-check.js asserts that all
three hand-typed lists in that workflow agree with it, and that every source is fit to be
mirrored at all (see the per-field notes below).
FIELDS
id             must equal the workflow's matrix `plugin:` value.
source         path to the skill directory, relative to the repo root.
repo           the GitHub repo the workflow rsyncs into.
installedName  what `npx skills add` installs it as; must equal SKILL.md frontmatter `name`.
sourceOwns     files at the mirror root that the PLUGIN owns and the rsync therefore
overwrites. Everything else at the mirror root (README.md, LICENSE,
.gitignore) is the mirror's own and is preserved. Declared, not guessed:
frontend-design's LICENSE.txt lives in the plugin and is derived, while
slopocop-code's LICENSE has no plugin counterpart and is furniture.
forbiddenTokens  substrings that must not appear anywhere under source. For a skill
published as ecosystem-free, this is the property that decides whether the
split was worth doing — a hand grep already missed one line once.
mirrored       false while a skill is being prepared for publication: its content is held
to every content rule, but the workflow is not yet expected to carry a row
for it. Content protection starts the day the skill is written, not the day
the workflow row lands — otherwise the first sync IS the first check.
